transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2026-07-09 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (CS), Maya (NorthShore), Omar (Platform), Liam (Security), Dina (PM)

Summary (auto): quick console demo focused on request forensics, trace playback, KV cache investigations, and security/compliance Qs.

===== Transcript =====
[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan, i'm here with priya and samir from redwood. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Maya: good, thanks. excited to go over the debug workflows, we've been seeing a few weird lat spikes and some inconsistent outputs.
[00:00:15] Jordan: perfect — objective today is to show how the console surfaces request logs, how you can replay traces, and how we surface kv / prefix cache hits so you can triage issues quickly. priya will drive demo.
[00:00:26] Priya: cool, i'll share my screen. first, quick context: northshore mentioned two main pain points — one is intermittent token-level latency spikes, and two is when the model hallucinated on a specific prompt set and you want to trace why.
[00:00:37] Omar: yes that's right, and we also need to prove to security that request payloads never leave our region for the pilot.
[00:00:41] Priya: got it. jump to the Requests tab. you can filter by model, route, status, and time window —
[00:00:48] [00:00:48] (screen actions) Priya: here is a request list, click into a single request to open the forensic view. you'll see a timeline on the right with token-by-token latency and trace spans.
[00:00:58] [00:00:58] Priya: notice the gray bars — those are batching wait times; the green is actual inference time. sometimes people assume higher token time = model slowness but it can be batching.
[00:01:10] Maya: oh interesting. can we pull the raw payload for a request?
[00:01:14] Priya: yes, raw payload is downloadable if you have the right RBAC. audit log will show who accessed it. there is also a redact option for PII at export.
[00:01:23] Liam: anything logged to cloud provider logs too or only the console? we need preserved audit trail for compliance.
[00:01:28] Jordan: we surface a full audit log (user, action, ip, timestamp), and for private deployments we can forward those to your SIEM or S3 bucket. we also integrate with SAML SSO — you can map roles to RBAC.
[00:01:41] Liam: good. KMS question: do embeddings or request payloads get encrypted with customer keys?
[00:01:46] Samir: short answer: for private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. for hosted dedicated we have an enterprise option to bring-your-own-keys; we will send the precise diagram and supported KMS providers.
[00:01:58] Omar: sweet. about the latency spikes — what does the console show for kv cache behavior?
[00:02:03] Priya: in the trace view we annotate KV cache hits and evictions. sometimes sequences that look similar don't hit prefix cache because of punctuation or whitespace differences. we also show approximate cache coverage % per model.
[00:02:16] Priya: right now we're seeing a 40% prefix cache hit rate on this workload, that explains some variability.
[00:02:23] Maya: and if the KV cache misses, does the runtime fall back to a smaller quantized model automatically?
[00:02:29] Priya: not automatically — policy driven. you can define routing fallbacks: region fallback, cheaper model variant, or queue to dedicated capacity. the console shows applied routing policy per request.
[00:02:39] Maya: hmm we need consistent latency under 120ms p95. does dedicated guarantee that?
[00:02:44] Jordan: dedicated gives you predictable throughput; we publish latency profiles for model variants. p95s depend on sequence length and batch size, but dedicated with reserved GPUs plus prewarming reduces variance.
[00:02:56] Omar: could we run a small benchmark from our payloads?
[00:02:59] Priya: yes — we have a benchmark runbook. i'll attach sample scripts. we'll also show how to interpret token-level latency in the run_results dashboard.
[00:03:08] (pause)
[00:03:14] Priya: demo - now i click "playback" on a request, you can step through each token generation and see the corresponding KV lookups, cache hit glyphs, and the kernel selection per layer — sometimes the runtime will pick a different kernel at longer seqs which affects warmup.
[00:03:29] Maya: interesting, i see a spike at token 38. what's that grey box at 38?
[00:03:34] Priya: that is a batching wait; if you expand the span details it shows the batch id and peers. you can then filter to see other requests that shared that batch.
[00:03:44] Omar: small tangent — we've got strict data residency: EU-only. can the hosted api pin to eu-west region?
[00:03:50] Jordan: yes, hosted with region pinning is available — for data residency requirements we recommend private (VPC) but hosted can be pinned to region and data not replicated elsewhere. we'll confirm retention and cross-region backups in the security doc.
[00:04:04] Liam: during playback, can we replay with redacted PII to reproduce the bug without exposing data?
[00:04:09] Priya: yes you can replay with sanitized payloads; we also have a "replay with mocks" mode so you can swap embeddings or context without leaking original vectors.
[00:04:19] Maya: you mentioned kernel selection — can that cause functional diffs between model variants?
[00:04:24] Priya: kernel selection is performance-level; functional diffs are possible if you're switching quantization or model variant. we surface model family and quantization profile per request so you can correlate quality regressions.
[00:04:36] Dina: can we tag requests that originate from a specific customer-facing product? we'd like to filter down by product id.
[00:04:41] Priya: yes, you can add custom metadata on the route and the SDK attaches app_id/app_version. those become queryable fields in the console.
[00:04:50] Maya: any way to automark problematic requests and create alerts?
[00:04:54] Samir: yep — set alert rules on error rate, latency p99, or specific mismatch metrics. alerts can create tickets in Jira or Slack.
[00:05:02] Omar: on the KV cache eviction patterns — is there a TTL we can tune?
[00:05:06] Priya: TTL and cache size are configurable per model group. also we provide recommendations via Redwood Optimize — it will suggest batch/window sizes and cache policies based on your workload.
[00:05:18] Maya: are there controls to avoid sensitive context being cached?
[00:05:21] Priya: yes, you can opt-out certain routes from prefix caching and set redaction rules.
[00:05:27] Liam: from security pov, we'd need proof that request payloads are not stored beyond retention windows — is retention configurable?
[00:05:33] Jordan: retention is configurable per account for hosted and fully managed in private. for enterprise contracts we can set custom retention and deletion SLAs.
[00:05:41] (small pause)
[00:05:56] Priya: quick detour — here's how to investigate a model-variant fallback: filter by status "fallback-used" then open the trace, it will show which variant served the request and why the policy triggered (e.g., capacity threshold exceeded).
[00:06:10] Maya: good. can we get a CSV export of all fallback events for the last 30 days?
[00:06:14] Priya: yes, export button exists and you can schedule recurring exports to an S3 or GCS bucket.
[00:06:20] Omar: are request IDs globally unique? we'd like to join them with our internal logs.
[00:06:24] Priya: yes, request IDs are UUIDs and we also allow you to pass a client_request_id that gets mirrored in the console.
[00:06:31] Liam: do we get token-level costs in the request view?
[00:06:34] Jordan: cost per token is surfaced at request level and in the cost breakdown dashboard. that helped another customer identify a spuriously long context that was costing them.
[00:06:42] Maya: okay this is all very helpful. how about an on-prem option? some of our data is air-gapped.
[00:06:46] Jordan: private on-prem is possible — there's an installation package and a private control plane. we can scope that as part of an enterprise contract; we should discuss timeline and infra requirements.
[00:06:57] Dina: what's the expected timeline to get a pilot running if we sign?
[00:07:01] Jordan: for hosted pilot with region pinning we can start in a week. for dedicated reserved capacity it's typically 2–4 weeks to provision. on-prem is longer — depends on infra availability.
[00:07:10] Maya: let's talk about the benchmark. can you walk through the runbook real quick?
[00:07:15] Priya: absolutely. we'll provide a lightweight harness: sample payload generator, sequence length distributions, parallel client stub. run it from your infra against our demo endpoint or bring your payloads to the dedicated environment. results upload to the run_results dashboard.
[00:07:29] Omar: are there limits on request replay rate? we don't want accidental DDoS of prod.
[00:07:34] Priya: playback requests are rate limited per account; there's also a dry-run mode that simulates timing without hitting the model.
[00:07:42] Liam: any legal or export restrictions we need to know about?
[00:07:45] Jordan: standard export controls apply. we'll include relevant notes in the legal package.
[00:07:50] Maya: one last thing — when you share the security pack can you include a sample data flow diagram and the list of sub-processors?
[00:07:56] Jordan: yes we'll include a network diagram, KMS flow, and sub-processor list.
[00:08:02] (demo wrap-up)
[00:08:10] Priya: quick recap of the demo flows — requests page, forensic view, playback, cache annotations, routing policy overlay, audit logs, and exports.
[00:08:18] Jordan: recap — next steps: security docs + KMS diagram, benchmark runbook, customer provides sample logs & residency requirements, schedule pilot kickoff.
[00:08:28] Maya: sounds good. any blockers on our side? not yet.
[00:08:31] Omar: none. we'll follow up on the pilot scope.
[00:08:35] Jordan: great, thanks everyone — we'll circulate notes and links.
[00:08:38] Samir: attaching links now in the calendar invite: (1) SOC2 + KMS doc, (2) benchmark runbook, (3) pilot checklist.
[00:08:46] Dina: thanks, bye.
[00:08:48] Jordan: thanks, bye.

Notes about transcription: occasional mistranscribes for acronyms (K V cache, S A M L) and some punctuation dropped. The demo included links: https://redwood.example.com/docs/soc2, https://drive.example.com/redwood-benchmark-runbook

End of transcript.
